item.title: [ecmascript] Map.prototype.has() refers to WeakMap instead of Map instance
item.content:encoded:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Map/has

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

Introduction

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

The introduction refers to the WeakMap instance instead of the Map instance

Map.prototype.has()
The has() method of WeakMap instances returns a boolean indicating whether an entry with the specified key exists in this WeakMap or not.

What did you expect to see?

It should refers to a Map instance

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

No response

Do you have anything more you want to share?

No response

item.title: [ecmascript] `null`: mention unusual `typeof` value on page
item.content:encoded:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/null

What did you expect to see?

Just a suggestion (I could see arguments that this isn't really relevant), but the null page could have a > [!NOTE] mentioning that despite being a primitive value, null has a typeof value of 'object' and linking to https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/typeof#typeof_null.

Not sure if this would make more sense by the undefined comparison (as this is a notable difference between the two values) or above.

item.title: [ecmascript] Yielding rejected promises from a sync generator now properly closes the iterator
item.content:encoded:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/for-await...of

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

From Note: until but not including Specification.

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

It seems at least modern Chrome does correctly call finally in the specified circumstances.

Assuming this is the case in all modern browsers and is perhaps even specified as such,
the corresponding content should be removed.

What did you expect to see?

No warning about an obsolete issue, assuming it actually is.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

Someone should check what the relevant spec says, I'm too busy, sorry.

Do you have anything more you want to share?

No response
